summary: A tense two-player card-driven wargame where battles are resolved not by dice but by whether you can play matching cards to keep your units loyal in the fight; the real game is a tight logistics puzzle of moving armies across the map while managing a shrinking, fluctuating hand of cards that represents your commanders' wavering allegiance. It plays fast for a wargame of its scope, with clean rules but deep, tense decision-making around when to commit forces to battle.
praised: Elegant, novel mechanics (no dice, cards as loyalty/movement fuel) that model historical uncertainty
Fast playtime and low rules overhead relative to typical wargames
High tension in deciding when to commit troops versus holding back
Strong two-player interaction and replayability from variable setup
Beautiful, functional map and component design
criticised: Steep initial learning curve to fully grasp the battle/deployment system
Can feel swingy if a key card isn't drawn at the right time
Some find the abstracted 'loyalty' battle resolution less satisfying than direct combat

interaction.kind: direct area-control conflict and blocking on a point-to-point map

scoring.why: The game ends immediately when one side captures enough enemy leaders/objectives or the other side's forces are exhausted, so there is no points tally at all
